meta.description: Cross-method decision tree for calling hits in pooled CRISPR screens. Catalogs statistical models (MAGeCK RRA, MAGeCK MLE, BAGEL2, drugZ, JACKS, Chronos, CERES), experimental designs each is built for, failure modes outside design domain, reconciliation when methods disagree, multiple-testing and effect-size thresholds, the order of operations, the second-best-sgRNA conservative rule, and consensus-hit strategy.

scientific_integrity.detail: All citations (Li 2014/2015, Hart 2017 G3, Colic 2019, Allen 2019, Dempster 2021, Meyers 2017) are real papers matching known CRISPR-screen literature; no fabricated DOI/PMID/statistics in any of the 7 outputs. All numeric results traced to real MAGeCK/BAGEL2/drugZ files or scripts executed for this audit.

practice_boundaries.detail: Purely gene-level/screen-level research analysis; no diagnostic or prescriptive claim about any individual across all 7 outputs; no disclaimer required for this research-only scope.

methodological_ground.detail: Real methodological gaps were found (Spearman sign/scale inversion in usage-guide.md's own prompt, Input 4; incomplete empty-consensus failure-mode list, Inputs 5/7), but none of the 7 delivered outputs itself asserted an inverted or fallacious conclusion -- each output caught and corrected the pitfall rather than being misled by it. The gaps are recorded as P1 recommendations rather than a veto.

code_usability.detail: All 3 Python code blocks embedded in SKILL.md parse (ast.parse). examples/consensus_hits.py ran unmodified against real HAP1 TKOv3 MAGeCK/BAGEL2 output with no errors. consensus_hits() and second_best_lfc(), adapted per SKILL.md's own text, ran cleanly on real data in Inputs 1, 3, 5.

functional_suitability.note: Broad, accurate coverage of 7 methods, reconciliation, consensus, and thresholds; one promised capability ('interpreting unstable hit lists across reruns', frontmatter) is entirely absent from the body (verified by grep), and three internal threshold defaults for the same MAGeCK-FDR/BAGEL-BF pair disagree with each other.

reliability.note: Between-method disagreement is well covered (explicit Trigger/Mechanism/Symptom/Fix tables); same-method rerun instability and cross-design file merges have no documented handling at all (verified via Inputs 5 and 6).

performance_context.note: Single 279-line SKILL.md plus a separate usage-guide.md and one example file; workflow is linear with no redundant round-trips.

agent_usability.note: Canonical decision-tree prompts resolve unambiguously to one correct, well-cited answer (Input 2); the internal threshold inconsistency and two unaddressed pitfalls (rerun instability, mismatched-design merge) are consistency and error-prevention gaps.

human_usability.note: Natural trigger phrasing throughout Quick Start and Example Prompts; advisory (non-CLI) nature is inherently forgiving of input variation.

security.note: No credentials, no injection vectors; example code snippets do no column/schema validation before use, so a malformed input file would raise a raw KeyError rather than a clear message.

maintainability.note: The same consensus logic is duplicated (with drifted default thresholds) between SKILL.md's inline function and examples/consensus_hits.py -- a concrete, demonstrated maintainability failure, not a hypothetical one.

agent_specific.note: Strong trigger precision and composability with the 4 upstream method Skills; idempotency and escape-hatch guidance both have real, demonstrated gaps (Inputs 5, 6, 7).

recommendations.title: BAGEL2 run-to-run non-determinism is unaddressed despite being named in scope
recommendations.problem: Two identical BAGEL.py bf runs on the same HAP1 TKOv3 data differ by up to 26.7 BF and flip 33 genes across the BF>6 threshold; this Skill's own frontmatter promises help 'interpreting unstable hit lists across reruns' but neither SKILL.md nor usage-guide.md mentions BAGEL2 seed management, reruns, or rerun variance anywhere.
recommendations.root_cause: The Reconciliation and Failure Modes tables cover disagreement BETWEEN methods only, never disagreement between two runs of the SAME method.
recommendations.fix: Add a row to the Reconciliation table for same-method rerun instability naming BAGEL2's -s/--seed requirement explicitly, and cross-link to bagel-essentiality's determinism guidance.

recommendations.title: Empty/degenerate consensus guidance omits the mismatched-design failure mode
recommendations.problem: Merging real MAGeCK+BAGEL2 essentiality results with a real drugZ table from an unrelated drug-response comparison produces an empty Tier-1 consensus even though the underlying screen has excellent QC (100% CEGv2/NEGv1 precision). SKILL.md's only documented cause for an empty 3-method consensus is poor screen quality, which would send a researcher to needlessly re-audit a healthy screen.
recommendations.root_cause: consensus_hits() and its usage-guide.md prompts never check or warn that merged files must come from the same experimental comparison.
recommendations.fix: Document 'mismatched comparison / wrong file' as an alternate cause of empty consensus alongside 'low screen quality', and add a same-design sanity check (e.g. comparing condition/replicate naming) before merging.

recommendations.title: Spearman rho audit prompt doesn't account for MAGeCK/BAGEL2 sign-scale inversion
recommendations.problem: usage-guide.md instructs computing Spearman rho between MAGeCK neg|score and BAGEL2 BF and auditing disagreement if rho<0.6. On real HAP1 TKOv3 data this rho is -0.806 (methods actually agree strongly once sign-corrected to +0.806), so literal application triggers a false 'disagreement' investigation.
recommendations.root_cause: MAGeCK neg|score is a p-value-like statistic (smaller=more essential) while BAGEL2 BF is a log-likelihood ratio (larger=more essential); the prompt never flags this inversion.
recommendations.fix: State explicitly in usage-guide.md that neg|score must be sign-flipped (or rank-reversed) before computing rho against BF, with a worked numeric example showing the real HAP1 values.

recommendations.title: Three different MAGeCK-FDR/BAGEL-BF threshold pairs across the Skill's own files
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's inline consensus_hits() defaults to FDR<0.05/BF>5; examples/consensus_hits.py defaults to FDR<0.1/BF>5; the Quantitative Thresholds table recommends FDR<0.05/BF>6. On real data this swings the 'consensus' gene count from 844 to 1131 (+34%) depending on which default is trusted.
recommendations.root_cause: The same two threshold numbers are hardcoded independently in three places that have drifted out of sync.
recommendations.fix: Make examples/consensus_hits.py and the inline SKILL.md function both default to the Quantitative Thresholds table's stated values (FDR<0.05, BF>6) and remove the duplicate hardcoding.

recommendations.title: second_best_lfc() silently exempts single-guide genes from its own rule
recommendations.problem: For any gene with only one sgRNA, second_best_lfc() falls back to that guide's own LFC, which then reads as 'passing' the second-best-sgRNA rule with no second guide involved at all. Not triggered on TKOv3 (always 4 guides/gene) but will silently misfire on sparser libraries.
recommendations.root_cause: No n_sgrnas>=2 guard or flag exists in the function.
recommendations.fix: Have second_best_lfc() return NaN or a 'single_guide' flag instead of a silently-passing fallback value when a gene has fewer than 2 sgRNAs.

recommendations.title: No references/ split for the dense 7-method comparison tables
recommendations.problem: All 7 methods' comparison tables, the reconciliation table, thresholds, and code live in one 279-line SKILL.md with no references/ subfolder, which is workable but denser than necessary for a single 'which method / how do I reconcile' query.
recommendations.root_cause: No references/ subfolder exists for this Skill, unlike some sibling Skills in the same folder.
recommendations.fix: Optionally split the Statistical Models Compared / Algorithmic Taxonomy tables into references/method-catalog.md, keeping SKILL.md focused on the decision tree and reconciliation workflow.
